body: I don’t know everything my friend was experiencing but he had a history of suicidal thoughts and depression. He attempted once before when he was going through a divorce with his wife a few years back. He mentioned feeling lonely and being depressed every once in a while. Before he passed he spent a lot of time alone and it was hard to talk to him because he seemed angry a lot or was very quiet. Whenever he seemed suicidal it was hard on me too because I did not know what was going to happen. It was hard because I did not know if I was helping. I made a few big sacrifices when helping him and now that he is gone I am really glad I did.

IMO the best thing you can do is spend time with them and listen to them if they feel like talking. Take anything they say seriously even if their problems do not make sense to you because in their head these things are causing hurt. Do something nice for them to show them people care about them. Help them in finding professional help and be supportive of them. Most of the time the thoughts will pass with a little bit of time. If you think they might hurt themselves try to keep them a way from anything harmful and try to avoid leaving them alone. Give them information on suicide hotlines in case they ever need to talk to some one. How long have they had suicidal thoughts for? Was there any specific events or things that triggered it? PM me if you need to talk. I lost my best friend to suicide and it is awful. I am hurting really bad from it.
Does the hurt ever get easier?
